title: Granular cursor encryption, resumable streaming, and migration guarantees for SDK clients
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: PRD for a cross-language client contract that introduces per-tenant encrypted cursors, resumable streaming sessions with checkpointing, and a clear migration strategy from legacy cursor formats. The goal is to enable safe cursor exchange across environments (hosted/dedicated/private), improve resumability of streaming APIs without duplicating events, and provide documented compatibility guarantees for Python/TS/Go SDKs so customers can upgrade with low risk.
requirements: Per-tenant cursor tokens: new cursor tokens must be envelope-wrapped and encrypted per-tenant using customer KMS where available; fallback to service-managed keys must be documented.
Cursor schema v2: include (a) sequence_checkpoint (monotonic integer), (b) partition_id (optional), (c) encrypted_payload (opaque), (d) schema_version="2" and backwards compatibility hints.
Resumable streaming: server must support resume requests that include the v2 cursor; SDKs must expose resume() ergonomics with transparent retry and de-duplication semantics.

Retry semantics: SDKs must implement idempotency-key based retries for non-streaming and per-chunk checkpoints for streaming. Exponential backoff with jitter recommended; default retry budget and max attempts documented and configurable.
Pagination mapping: Servers must accept legacy cursor formats and return a migration_hint header on first compatible request; clients must detect and surface migration_hint to operators.

Compatibility guarantees: minor releases (x.y) cannot change public method signatures or remove fields from persisted cursors; major releases (x) may introduce breaking change with 90-day deprecation window and automated migration tooling.

Language parity: Python/TS/Go SDKs will have equivalent surface area for streaming resume, cursor encryption toggles, and pagination helpers; naming may follow idiomatic conventions but behavior must match tests in the conformance suite.

Observability: SDKs must emit structured telemetry (events) for resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_fallback, cursor_migration_detected, and cursor_decryption_failure including tenant_id and truncated cursor hash (not raw cursor).
scope_changes: Initial scope included server-side only cursor encryption. Added client toggles and CLI migration tool after security review recommended visible opt-out and operator migration path.
Streaming checkpoint granularity: changed from per-message checkpointing to configurable per-chunk (default 1KB roughly equivalent) to reduce overhead after perf profiling.
Deprecated plan to auto-upgrade legacy cursors in-place: switched to opt-in migration with a CLI to avoid accidental cross-region key access during rotation.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs (Python/TS/Go) have unit tests in conformance suite that validate: resume from v2 cursor yields ordered, non-duplicated events for 10k message replay with simulated transient disconnects.
CI test that injects a legacy cursor (v1) and verifies server returns migration_hint header and the TypeScript SDK surfaces a one-line warning to the operator.

End-to-end test with service-managed keys and KMS-backed tenant keys that confirms cursor encryption/decryption and that encrypted cursors for one tenant cannot be decrypted under another tenant id (negative test).
Canary in production: 5% of traffic routed to runtime with v2 cursors enabled; monitor resume_success >= 99.5% and resume_latency P95 < 250ms for resume path during canary window.

Backward compatibility: minor version bump of each language SDK validated by running downstream internal apps (tracking two representative product teams) with no runtime exceptions for cursor handling.
Docs: Migration guide, API reference, and example snippets for Python/TS/Go published in docs repo before release and linked from SDK release notes.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (SDKs + Server): Add v2 cursor support and return migration_hint when v1 cursor is observed. Default behavior: accept v1 and respond normally; do not rewrite cursors.

Phase 2 (Operator tooling): Release 'redwood-cursor-migrate' CLI that takes a list of v1 cursors and emits v2 encrypted tokens using tenant KMS/key material; CLI supports dry-run and audit log output.

Phase 3 (Client opt-in): SDKs expose 'auto_migrate_cursors' flag disabled by default; enabling will call migration endpoint once per unique cursor and replace persisted cursor in-place with v2 returned by server; log migration events.

Phase 4 (Deprecation): After 90 days and verified metrics, announce deprecation of v1 read support in the hosted product with clear calendar date; customers using Dedicated/Private get separate timeline and self-hosted migration script.
sdk_examples:
Python example (resume streaming):

from redwood import StreamingClient
client = StreamingClient(api_key=... , tenant_id=...)
stream = client.resume_stream(cursor="v2:eyJzZXFfdG9rZW4iOiAxMjMgfQ==")
for msg in stream:
    process(msg)

# config: client = StreamingClient(..., auto_migrate_cursors=False, retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_attempts=5))
testing_and_validation: Conformance suite: add cross-language tests that fuzz cursor blobs (valid, truncated, invalid signature) to ensure deterministic error codes and no sensitive leak in logs.
Chaos testing: simulate server process restart during streaming and verify all SDKs resume and dedupe within 3 attempts; record success/failure rates in the canary dashboard.
Security audit: run static analysis on CLI and SDK code paths that handle raw cursor bytes; ensure no logging of unredacted cursor contents and encryption keys are never serialized to logs.
Load test: exercise pagination and resume endpoints with 1000 concurrent tenants and verify server-side CPU and memory growth is linear and within SLOs.
rollout_plan: Developer preview: internal SDK alpha for product and platform teams (2 weeks) to gather feedback on ergonomics and error messages.
Limited public beta: enable for self-serve tenants with explicit opt-in and guidance (4 weeks); monitor metrics and support tickets.
Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over two weeks with target success metrics; pause if resume_success drops below 99% or errors spike >2x baseline.
Final GA: publish SDK minor versions and CLI; include deprecation notice for v1 cursor read-without-migration and final timeline.
